User manual

The three-cushion assistant, step by step

This manual teaches you to operate the application from start to finish, in the order you will use it: place the balls, declare the shot, read what the app draws, and get the most out of every system and tool. Read it with the app open beside you: each chapter is a set of steps you can execute right away.

01

First steps: the table and the balls

The digital table reproduces a professional table: playing surface of 284 × 142 cm cushion to cushion, with a 5 cm inner blue band and a 9 cm wooden rail. Departure and attack are read projected onto the central axis of the diamonds, just as on the real table.

  1. Drag the balls with the mouse or your finger to the position you want to study. The route recalculates itself with every move.
  2. For exact positions, open "Place the balls by measuring distances to the cushions" and type the distances in centimeters (period or comma both work). The ball moves as you type.
  3. On touch screens, enable touch mode: each ball offers fine-nudge buttons so you can adjust without covering the table with your finger.
02

Cue ball and calculation system

  1. Choose the cue ball: white or yellow. All calculations, labels and warnings use the chosen ball as the departure ball.
  2. Choose the calculation system for the shot: LKL / Base 50 for routes of up to three cushions with departure, arrival and attack readings; Plus for short → long → long patterns with the third long cushion as the zero cushion; and Mirror (halves) for any cushion combination, with the stroke physics declared and the complete carom (chapter 06).
03

Declaring the shot sequence

  1. Choose the departure: "Cushion first, then ball" (the cue ball visits cushions before the first contact) or "Ball first, then cushions".
  2. Choose the first ball: a specific one, or the virtual point between the two non-cue balls for kisses and position play.
  3. Declare the cushions of the sequence in order. The app blocks physically impossible combinations: two identical consecutive cushions cannot be selected, except when an intermediate ball separates them (chapter 06).
  4. If you only want to record or photograph free positions, use "No plan": the table stays clean of routes.
04

Working with LKL / Base 50

  1. With the sequence declared, read in the diagnosis the calculated departure, arrival and attack point, projected onto the diamonds.
  2. Apply Roger Conti's side spins (levels 0 to 4, half a tip per level): the app shows the built-in visual reference and adjusts the reading. The chosen level stays visible in the module.
  3. Enable the informative connectors (3→4 in the references module; 4→5 and 5→6 in the header, according to direction R to L or L to R). They are a reading layer: they help you see continuations without modifying the calculated attack.
05

Working with Plus

  1. Select Plus for short → long → long patterns with the third long cushion as the zero cushion.
  2. Read the system's own numbering along the rail and the physical attack point the app marks on the cushion: the number and the spot where you must attack, with the resulting route drawn on the table.
06

Working with Mirror (halves)

The Mirror calculates by exact geometric unfolding and declares its contract: rolling ball (center or half a tip above), no side spin, natural rolling speed. Everything it draws follows from that contract or from the alternate contracts described below.

  1. Calibrate your table's coefficient (once): set up a known slanted rebound and strike at center ball. If the ball arrives long relative to the line, raise the slider; if short, lower it. The value is saved in your browser and shared by the four language versions. The engine applies it with angular intelligence, following a curve measured on a real table.
  1. Complete carom in cushion-first: when you pick a specific ball, the selector speaks in carom ("Yellow, then red"): the first is the waypoint and the second the destination. The app computes the exact point on the waypoint, draws it as a dashed ghost, notes the fullness, and recalculates the first attack toward that take, with two decimals.
  1. Choose the carom route: three straight cushions, or the two intermediate-ball variants (the carom demands three cushions before the third ball, not before the second). With the ball in between, the cushion before and after the contact can be the same one: the selectors enable the repeat only where it is legal.
  1. Read the ladder notices: if the rolling ball reaches (≈34° cone), ghost and fullness with full authority and a clean board. If not, the app computes the tangent take: an amber notice warns that it demands stun or check, the fullness carries its label and the attack is recalculated. And if not even the tangent suffices, it draws through centers and leaves the fullness to your judgment, saying so plainly. The dashed leg of the degraded rungs is the geometric requirement, not a prediction; every notice carries the link to the full physics of the module.
  1. In ball-first, choose the strike at contact: "Rolling" (departure inside the cone, fullness from contact physics) or "Stun / tangent" (perpendicular departure, up to 90°, for what rolling forbids). The app warns if the contact is too thin, too full, or at the physical limit.
07

Placing balls from a photograph

  1. Take or load a photo of the table from the photo module.
  2. Mark the four corners of the cloth in the order the app indicates.
  3. Mark the three balls on the image.
  4. Press calculate: the app transfers the positions to the digital table, ready for declaring the shot.
08

Overhead camera and automatic detector

With a fixed camera above the table, the app captures positions without touching the phone: always the same framing, an almost perpendicular view.

  1. Install the camera and run the app's overhead validation (geometric certification of the framing).
  2. Use automatic capture: the app photographs the table, and the detector proposes table and balls.
  3. Review and confirm the proposed points; the camera's real resolution is reported on screen.
09

Video of the shot with overlaid data

  1. Calibrate the four corners of the video once per session.
  2. Record the stroke: the app overlays the calculated plan (attack, ghost, route and numbered discs) on the real footage.
  3. Review the shot in slow motion or frame by frame, and export the MP4 with the data burned in, ready to share.
10

Tips and troubleshooting

  1. After an app update, reload with Ctrl+Shift+R (or clear the browser cache) to receive the new version.
  2. The Mirror coefficient is saved per browser and per site: if you change device or browser, calibrate again (one minute).
  3. If a cushion selector appears disabled, physics is right: two identical consecutive cushions are only legal with an intermediate ball declared in the route.
  4. If the app says "no geometric solution", it is not an error: that sequence does not exist from those positions. Try another route, other cushions or another position.
  5. Whenever an amber notice appears, read the diagnosis and follow its explanation link: the full physics of the module lives there.
